_note: Core/Device (parity/F06-device.md), BATTERY and THERMAL. Two things are pinned. First the folds: battery status to the four state words, and Android's seven thermal levels onto the four the contract uses (iOS reports exactly those four, so the fold is one-directional). Second, and more important, the DELIVERY RULE: every value here is event driven on all three renderers. A module that polls the battery is a module that drains it, so a runner must assert that no timer is registered by this module and that a value change arrives from the platform's own callback.
_runner: No runner is wired yet (registration is in the F06 handoff).

state.name: plugged in but not charging is still unplugged to a caller: it is not gaining charge
a platform that will not say reports unknown, never a guess
no battery at all: state unknown and the level field is ABSENT, not zero

level.name: an unreadable level is absent, and -1 in the context var

thermal.name: a platform with no thermal API omits the field rather than reporting nominal

delivery._note: The no-polling assertion. A runner drives the platform's own callback and asserts the context var moved, then asserts the module registered no timer or interval of its own.

cases.name: a battery level change from the platform callback updates batteryLevel
entering low power mode updates lowPowerMode
no callback, no work: nothing is scheduled while the values are steady
